question: Does changing only the production CUDA F4 update-grid target from four to six resident blocks per RTX 5090 SM materially reduce primary device time without a greater-than-two-percent complete-stage or holdout regression?

claims.text: Both arms reproduce every registered matrix shape, rank, refuted result, pinned count, and word-operation count exactly.
claims.if_not_supported: the session is invalid and no timing or mechanism claim is admitted

claims.text: The six-block target improves primary k0n13m2d6 device-stage time by at least two percent on the registered RTX 5090 session.
claims.if_supported: report a device-stage engineering speedup scoped to this exact session
claims.if_not_supported: do not retain the production candidate for performance

claims.text: The six-block target has no greater-than-two-percent complete-stage regression on any registered cell and no greater-than-two-percent device-stage regression on any non-primary cell.
claims.if_supported: the candidate passes the prospective non-regression family
claims.if_not_supported: the candidate is rejected even if the primary point estimate improves

claims.text: Nsys shows exactly the registered four-to-six-block update-grid transformation while launch order, all non-update geometry, and update resource use remain fixed.
claims.if_supported: the observed timing comparison has the registered mechanism
claims.if_not_supported: the session is invalid for the geometry claim

hypotheses.statement: More update blocks expose additional independent work on the primary matrix without changing arithmetic work.
hypotheses.mechanism: The update kernel remains at 256 threads, 31 registers per thread, 16 KiB static shared memory, and zero local bytes per thread; six blocks fill the RTX 5090's 48-warp per-SM limit when enough tiles exist.

predictions.minimum_effect: median paired baseline/candidate speedup >= 1.02 and simultaneous lower bound > 1 on k0n13m2d6

data_seen.measured: v7 baseline showed update as 51.7% of primary kernel time; no six-block candidate data existed

provenance.decisive_scope: all v8 rows are fresh; v7 selected the mechanism but supplied no candidate outcome

arms.description: The candidate commit build-closure archive with only suite/src/cryptanalysis/f4_gpu.rs overlaid from the retained v7 production commit, preserving the four-block-per-SM target.
The same candidate commit build-closure archive without an overlay, containing only the registered six-block-per-SM production change relative to the constructed baseline tree.

aa.not_applicable_reason: The immediately preceding frozen v7 run is a retained byte-identical A/A noise calibration on the same Secure RTX 5090 five-cell path. V8 spends its single allocation on the one-factor A/B and does not reuse any v7 timing row in its distribution.

positive.not_applicable_reason: Every execution is a deterministic known-answer control; any shape, answer, or work mismatch invalidates the session before timing is interpreted.

negative.not_applicable_reason: This fixed-input engineering comparison makes no discovery, detector-yield, or population claim.

measurement.timed_primary_justification: The optimization changes launch geometry while exact word_ops is invariant, so counts cannot measure scheduling or memory-latency effects. A clock is admitted only for successful fresh-process rows inside one same-pod alternating session that earn tierB by the frozen numeric PSI, throttle, memory-event, steal, temperature, identity, and no-foreign-process gates.

stopping_rules.rule: Attempt exactly one warmup and six measured fresh-process pairs for every registered cell, followed by exactly one primary Nsys capture per arm.
Stop and retain the session on any source, identity, correctness, isolation, process, profiler, archive, or cleanup gate failure; do not replace the pod or row.
The provider controller may create at most one pod and maximum cost exposure is USD 3.57.

invalidation_rules: Any source archive, overlay, scoped diff, tooling, binary, protocol, GPU identity, or arm identity mismatch invalidates the session.
Any missing, duplicate, retried, resumed, failed, non-CUDA, wrong-answer, wrong-work, or wrong-order execution invalidates the session.

Any measured row with CPU PSI some avg10 >10, CPU PSI full avg10 !=0, memory PSI some/full avg10 !=0, a cgroup throttle/memory-event delta, a steal delta, GPU temperature >=90 C, a foreign GPU process, or malformed telemetry is invalid.
Any Nsys trace without exactly 2,941 ordered update launches, exact four-versus-six grid formula, identical non-update geometry, or exact update resources invalidates the session.
Any profile duration entering the timing distribution invalidates the analysis.
A missing experiment.export/v1, rows.jsonl, analysis.json, transport receipt, archive manifest, or exact-ID cleanup absence check makes the session incomplete.

decision_rule.text: First require every source, execution, exact-answer, exact-work, numeric-isolation, telemetry, Nsys mechanism, export, transport, and cleanup gate. Enumerate all 6^6 paired resamples for each registered timing metric using exact Fractions and the median of paired baseline/candidate ratios. For a ten-test one-sided Bonferroni family at alpha .05, take the sorted bootstrap order statistic at floor(46656/200), zero based. geometry_supported requires the primary device median >=51/50 and lower >1, plus median and lower >=50/51 for complete_ms on all five cells and device_ms on all four non-primary cells. Any failed timing gate yields geometry_not_supported; an exact or isolation failure yields invalid_measurement; missing required completion artifacts yields incomplete_session.
decision_rule.threshold: primary device median >=51/50 and simultaneous lower >1; nine non-regression medians and lower bounds >=50/51
decision_rule.statistic: median of six paired baseline/candidate ratios; exact ordinary paired bootstrap of that median over all 6^6 resamples
decision_rule.interval: ten simultaneous one-sided lower bounds using exact Bonferroni lower-tail quantile 1/200; no RNG or floating-point comparison
